findings.title: TTL boundary and revocation behaviour are untested
findings.description: api/permissions.py adds 10 lines of new branching logic with no test change. Untested observable paths: a first call (cache miss) vs. an immediate second call (hit), behaviour exactly at the TTL boundary, and the sequence allow -> revoke -> call-again, which currently still returns allow. The last of these is observable to a caller and is the behaviour most likely to be assumed correct.
findings.suggested_action: Add tests for cache miss, cache hit, the TTL boundary, and allow-then-revoke, with time injected rather than relying on wall-clock sleeps.

findings.title: Cached decision makes tests order-dependent
findings.description: Module-level cache state persists between tests in the same process, so a test that grants access will leak a cached allow into any later test using the same (user_id, resource_id). Suites will pass or fail depending on execution order.
findings.suggested_action: Expose a reset hook or make the cache injectable so each test starts from a known state.
